verdict: Conditionally feasible as a durable obligation journal and constrained IaC view; arbitrary HCL and generic immutable-artifact adoption are not established.

evidence.context7: Monthly quota exceeded; used official docs and pinned source directly.

strongest_findings: AWS s3_object metadata edits take an upload branch; absent source/content selects empty bytes. Source evidence, not cloud execution.
Versioned aws_s3_object destruction calls deletion of all versions of the key; version_id is computed, not configurable.
Sensitive output values survive in structured output, state backups, synthetic copies and logs after current-state tombstoning.
Removing a declaration bypassed prevent_destroy and omitted its destroy-time provisioner; the sandbox artifact survived.
Same HCL without file dependencies failed; two local module instances shared and overwrote path.module output.
Same HCL without operational state generated a different binding identity.
user_judgments: Constrained HCL admission versus opaque arbitrary effects
Erasure assurance and allowable surviving metadata/copies
Retention overrides, replacement authorization and independence methodology
next_experiment: Separately authorized disposable S3 import/metadata/version/deletion tests; otherwise fake-provider byte-preservation and retained-identity plan gate.
limitations: No cloud calls, remote backend, actual DML integration, concurrent deployment or secure storage-page erasure test.
